prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Regional Dispatch Center (call sign Juniper), primary EMS dispatch: intake, triage, ambulance dispatch, coverage picture from unit locations, crew reports, readiness. Zones have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center; gaps escalated/reassessed. Juniper creates incident record, produces Unit Staging Change Card, records authorization time/selection reason; uses Battery Swap Voucher to confirm battery readiness before service; uses North Approach Queue Snapshot for northern congestion before routing; uses Caller Location Correction Slip to reconcile destination changes with incident record; records approved alternative routes ensuring critical-area coverage; evaluates destination consultation outcome vs acuity, transport time, coverage. Actors: Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): location first, repeat-back; produces correction slip; confirms incident ID and receiving facility before destination request. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): sets priority; escalates to Regional Medical Director; sends Pediatric Acuity Note; advises repositioning on demand changes. Regional Medical Director: clinical guidance/priorities for elevated demand and specialized destinations; no dispatch authority. Dispatcher: recommends units; states constraints; compares response times with remaining coverage before moving units. Shift Commander (Sundial): operational authority, surge, staging approval; sends Mutual Aid Release Form; must not override clinical policy/crew judgment. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): talkgroup, transmits assignments over Regional Radio Network; retries/alerts supervisor; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Paramedic Crew: acknowledges, reports status and unsuitable routes (closure, unsafe, delay). Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): capacity info, coordinates destination consultation, confirms with Emergency Department (which advises capacity/access/status), records outcome, sends restrictions to Juniper; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): vehicle restrictions, maintenance clearance; produces Battery Swap Voucher. Data Quality Officer (Pebble): reviews inconsistencies, routes corrections; sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo; no priority changes. Systems: Computer Aided Dispatch Console; Ambulance Coordination Platform (unit status, time-stamped history, presents approved destination/instructions); Ambulance Unit 417; Regional Radio Network; North Gate Status Board (queue snapshot, latest queue/access restriction); South Gate Status Board. Process: triage, selection, controlled handoff after acknowledgment.

Document units:
S159: The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
S160: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
S161: The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
S162: The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
S163: The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
S164: The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
S165: Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
S166: Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
S167: Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
S168: The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
S169: The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
S170: The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
S171: The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
S172: The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
S173: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
S174: Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
S175: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
S176: Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
S177: Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
S178: Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
S179: Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
S180: Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.
